# LatentRefusal: Latent-Signal Refusal for Unanswerable Text-to-SQL Queries

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#latentrefusal)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1007.pdf) · Findings of ACL 2026 proceedings, pages 20162-20179

**Reading coverage:** All eighteen PDF pages, Sections 1-5, limitations/ethics and Appendices A-E; equations, tables, algorithms and translated screenshot examples covered.

## Research question

Refusal based on generated text or repeated SQL samples can be costly and can happen after questionable SQL has already been produced.

## Method

A frozen local LLM provides intermediate activations to a supervised Tri-Residual Gated Encoder. A thresholded answerability score controls SQL generation. The probe adds attention, feed-forward and SwiGLU residual branches; its development-set selection is deployment-specific.

## Evaluation

Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B are evaluated on four separately trained dataset groups, including ambiguity, TriageSQL, reading comprehension and a nonpublic enterprise set. Each dataset has a sampled 300-example test set; architecture and layer ablations use TriageSQL.

## What the results support

Average F1 is reported as 88.5% and 88.8%. TRGE improves over the tested pooled/linear and latent baselines, but not every model-dataset cell is best. Probe-only latency is a few milliseconds; it excludes the backbone forward pass.

## Limits and qualifications

White-box activations and new-domain supervised adaptation are required. The semantic-entropy SQL baseline uses syntactic agreement. Appendix algorithms for additional hallucination detection and domain-specific probes are explicitly outside the main results. Safe refusal labels do not certify correctness of admitted SQL.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Supports efficient pre-generation screening, with a clear boundary between answerability prediction and semantic verification.
